= Cloud July 31, 2026

[NOTE]
====
Kobiton now uses date-based release versioning. Instead of version numbers such as 4.26S or 4.19.3, releases are identified by the build date in YYYYMM.DD format. For example, 202607.31 represents a build created on July 31, 2026.

Cloud release notes are typically published weekly and summarize changes since the previous publication. +
Version information for individual software components is available in the Component versions section.
====

== Kobiton MCP server

- Skills that cannot run on the current host now fail immediately and name the missing requirement: local file access, a local binary, or a specific platform. Previously, the skill started and failed part-way through with an error that gave no indication of the cause.

// REVIEWER NOTE:
// KOB-54047 | Team: DLM | Deployment: Cloud | ship_date: 2026-07-31 | bucket_source: updated_fallback
// bucket:updated — verify. Components: MCP server, Plugin. Kept under MCP filter as major (new enforcement mechanism).
// Reworded at final review — bullets now describe the change from the caller's point of view
// (clear, early failure with a reason) rather than the declare/enforce mechanism.

== Reports

- Fixed the Usage Report summary cards showing value rows cut off in the new UI. Values now render fully.

// REVIEWER NOTE:
// KOB-53958 | Team: DLM | Deployment: Cloud | ship_date: 2026-07-27 | bucket_source: updated_fallback
// bucket:updated — verify. Component: Reporting.
// FINAL: ok to include

== Device passcode

- Passcode configuration now takes effect the first time a device connects. Previously, it applied only after a deviceConnect service restart.

// REVIEWER NOTE:
// KOB-52048 | Team: DLM | Deployment: Cloud | ship_date: 2026-07-28 | bucket_source: resolutiondate
// Component: Passcode.
// Reworded at final review — the user-visible win is that no deviceConnect restart is needed for
// passcode configuration to be populated. Dropped the internal `DeviceConfiguration` object name.

== Scriptless Test Runs

- Improved step labeling for Test Cases converted from automation sessions. Test Cases display descriptive step names such as `Tap` and `Press Back`, while Scriptless Test Runs display the corresponding automation commands (for example, `/click` and `/back`). This makes it easier to trace executed steps back to the original automation script.
